question: How much residual moisture did the water-processed NMC532 cathode lose between 20 °C and drying at 120 °C, and how does its final value compare with the NMP-processed cathode dried at 100 °C?
expect: 625 to 47 ppm: 578 ppm removed; NMP-processed at 100 °C: 87 ppm, so the water-based cathode ends lower (p8.L53-59)
rendered:
According to the text, the water-processed NMC532 cathode initially contained 625 ppm of residual moisture at 20 °C. After drying at 120 °C, the residual moisture was reduced to 47 ppm. 

The NMP-processed NMC532 cathode, on the other hand, contained 200 ppm of residual moisture at 20 °C and was reduced to 87 ppm after drying at 100 °C. 

Therefore, the water-processed cathode lost 578 ppm of residual moisture (625 ppm - 47 ppm), while the NMP-processed cathode lost 113 ppm of residual moisture (200 ppm - 87 ppm).
